newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Corp wins Y25 bln HK ship order.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Corp wins Y25 bln HK ship order.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp said on Tuesday it had received an order for 10 double-hull cargo ships worth about 25 billion yen from Top Glory Shipping Co Ltd, a Hong Kong-based shipping company.
The order comprises six 30,000-tonne bulk carriers and four 74,000-tonne, or Panamax-sized, vessels, a Sumitomo spokesman said.
The ships will be built by Oshima Shipbuilding Co Ltd, a medium-sized shipbuilder based in Nagasaki prefecture, southern Japan, Sumitomo said in a statement.
Oshima is 50-percent owned by Osaka Shipbuilding Co Ltd, 25 percent owned by Sumitomo Heavy Industries Ltd and 25 percent owned by Sumitomo Corp, it said.
The ordered ships will be delivered in 1998 and 1999, the spokesman said.
Top Glory was established by Chinese state company China National Cereals Oils & Foodstuffs Import & Export Corp, Sumitomo said.
Sumitomo, one of Japan's leading trading companies, said it would jointly operate the four Panamax-sized vessels with Top Glory.
Top Glory, which had been relying on charter ships, decided to establish its own fleet in 1994 as its business grew in line with China's economic growth, Sumitomo said.
